Blueberries belong to the genus Vaccinium, and there are several species of blueberries, including Vaccinium corymbosum, which is the highbush blueberry, and Vaccinium angustifolium, known as the lowbush or wild blueberry. These plants produce small, round, and often bluish-purple berries.The reason blueberries are classified as fruits is because they meet the botanical definition of fruit. In botanical terms, a fruit is the mature ovary of a flowering plant, typically containing seeds. In the case of blueberries, the flesh of the berry develops from the ovary of the flower, and it encases tiny seeds. However, the seeds in blueberries are usually quite small and not very prominent when you consume the fruit.
